- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment shows early positive spikes (e.g., 0.20–0.40), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion term.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay correction until 2–3 periods post-spike.
- In low-sentiment environments, model exhibits persistent upward bias; apply smoothing or decay filter to forecast trend.
- When sentiment is absent or flat, model’s 30-day forecast often diverges from true outcome; use 18-day history as anchor for correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model tends to hold high forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 periods post-peak.
- Sentiment > 0.20 correlates with higher volatility; model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance or add stochastic component.
